results_section: 1. These savings are not marginal: in the Matrix Multiplication task at the largest scale, the selected candidate reduced energy consumption by more than 98%.
2. For example, the selected candidate for Array Sum (at a scale of 104 elements) was 11.49% more energy-efficient than the fastest alternative.
3. The improvements relative to the Top-1 baseline (p < 0.001) were found to be statistically significant.
4. The improvements relative to the Best-Time baseline (p = 0.0039) were found to be statistically significant.
5. our measurement protocol yielded high consistency, with an average coefficient of variation across five repeated runs of only 8.62% for runtime.
6. our measurement protocol yielded high consistency, with an average coefficient of variation across five repeated runs of only 10.75% for energy.
7. A few outliers exhibited minor slowdowns, with the largest penalty observed being approximately 0.023 seconds in the JSON Parsing task.
8. As noted in the evaluation summary, only three out of ten tasks (30%) retained the same optimal variant across all tested sizes.
